title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore says 'Last Full Backup: Aug 2, 2026 10:30' — same app, same second, same fact
what_happened: The scratch instance ran its startup backup check at 10:27:45 local: three .nsbackup files were written and app_settings got autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:27:45.635595Z. I then opened Settings > Files & Storage at 10:28 and scrolled to Status. At 10:30:02 the card still read 'Last backup / Never' with the trailing status 'Pending'. Clicking 'Back Up Now' immediately corrected it to 'Last backup / 0s ago' and 'In 23h', so the widget can render a real value — it just never picks up the backup the app itself performed. STRONGER REPRO: I then restarted the app (same profile, same DB). With autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:30:25.957100Z persisted and four .nsbackup files on disk, a freshly opened Settings > Files & Storage again reads 'Last backup / Never' and 'Pending'. So the persisted timestamp is never hydrated into the card at all; the only thing that makes it truthful is pressing Back Up Now in the current session, and that truth is lost on the next launch. DIRECT CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO SURFACES: in the same session and within seconds of each other, Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore > Auto-Save Status reads 'Last Full Backup: Aug 2, 2026 10:30' and lists the real files under Recent Backups, while Settings > GENERAL > Files & Storage > Status reads 'Last backup / Never' and 'Pending'. Backup & Restore hydrates from the persisted key correctly; Files & Storage does not.
expected: The Status card must reflect the persisted autosave.last_backup_at (and any backup completed in this session). 'Never' is a false statement about the user's data-protection state: the natural reaction is to assume backups are broken, or to conclude they are working when they are not.
repro: Press 'Back Up Now' (card correctly shows '7m ago' / 'In 23h'), then stop and relaunch the app with the same profile and reopen Settings > Files & Storage: the card is back to 'Never' / 'Pending' while sqlite3 app_settings still holds autosave.last_backup_at and the .nsbackup files are still on disk.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/07-files-scroll.png ('Last backup / Never', trailing 'Pending') taken at 10:30:02; sqlite3 app_settings autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:27:45.635595Z; ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups shows skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-45.572326.nsbackup. After clicking Back Up Now the tree reads 'Status / 0s ago' + 'In 23h' and the key becomes 14:30:25.957100Z. After restart (pid 2190911): tree shows 'panel: Status / panel: Never / panel: Last backup / panel: Pending' while sqlite3 gives autosave.last_backup_at|2026-08-02T14:30:25.957100Z and ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups holds 4 files from this run. Same-session comparison: tree of ADVANCED > Backup & Restore = 'Auto-Save Status / Last Sequence Save Never / Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 10:30' plus a Recent Backups list containing skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-30-25.892145.nsbackup; tree of GENERAL > Files & Storage taken immediately after = 'panel: Status / panel: Never / panel: Last backup / panel: Pending'. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/46-backup-restore.png.
location_wrong: auto_save_service.dart:149-166 is NOT where the bug is — that block is correct, carries a comment describing this exact symptom, and publishes the hydrated status. The hydration never reaches the instance the page sees: autoSaveServiceProvider (auto_save_service.dart:690) `ref.watch(backendProvider)`, so the service is rebuilt on a backend swap, while autoSaveLifecycleProvider — the only caller of start(config, lastBackup) — is read once, unawaited, at apps/desktop/lib/main.dart:280 and is never watched afterwards. start() also begins `if (_started) return;`, so a service started without arguments can never be hydrated later. Fix site is the provider wiring / the page's ref.watch at auto_save_settings.dart:179.
proposed_fix: Make Files & Storage read the same source Backup & Restore already reads (autoSaveStatusProvider, which seeds from the persisted autosave.last_backup_at) instead of the raw service status.
verdict_reasoning: Both halves reproduced. (1) SAME-SESSION CONTRADICTION: with app_settings holding autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T16:03:47.621627Z (12:03 local, written by this process), Settings > GENERAL > Files & Storage > Status read 'Last backup / Never' + 'Pending' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/23-files2.png), while Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore in the same session showed 'Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 12:03' plus a Recent Backups list of real .nsbackup files. (2) 'Back Up Now' corrected the card to '0s ago' / 'In 23h' and the key became 16:15:01.581767Z. (3) STRONGER REPRO HELD: after stop+start on the same profile, with the key still 16:15:01.581767Z, Files & Storage again renders 'Never' / 'Pending' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/24-post-restart.png). P1 stands: a false 'Never' about data protection is the cry-wolf class, and one of the two surfaces is lying at all times.

title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them — every displayed time silently stays on the host's timezone
what_happened: Settings > Location > Time: I turned 'Use system time' OFF and set Timezone = America/Los_Angeles, then Asia/Tokyo, then UTC. app_settings.timezone and use_system_time persist correctly each time, but NOTHING on screen changes: the status-bar clock stayed 14:44 (host America/New_York) when it should have read 11:44 PDT / 03:44 JST / 18:44 UTC, the Dashboard header clock stayed host-local, and the Dashboard twilight strip stayed byte-identical (Sunset 23:48 / Astro dark 02:00 / Astro dawn 06:31 / Sunrise 08:43) across all three timezones. Root cause in source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/clock_provider.dart:219 _parseTimezoneOffset accepts only 'UTC' or 'UTC+HH[:MM]' and returns null for anything else, so clockProvider falls back to SystemClock for all 17 IANA entries the picker offers. The fallback is completely silent — the file's own comment claims 'Failure to parse is explicit and logged at the Clock.fromUtc call sites', but nothing appears in app.log (grep for timezone/clock/tz over the whole 151-line log: zero hits).
expected: Picking a site timezone must change displayed times, or the picker must not exist. clockProvider feeds imaging_service capture timestamps, session_provider and scheduler_provider, so a remote-observatory operator who sets the site timezone gets host-local timestamps on their frames and host-local scheduler decisions while the UI shows the timezone they chose.
repro: Settings > Location, scroll to Time. Toggle 'Use system time' OFF. Set Timezone = Asia/Tokyo. Look at the status-bar clock and at Dashboard > twilight strip. Repeat with America/Los_Angeles and UTC.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/24-status.png (LA, sys-time on: 14:43), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/25-status.png (LA, sys-time OFF: 14:44 — unchanged), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/27-status.png (Asia/Tokyo, sys-time OFF: 14:44), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/31-status.png (UTC, sys-time OFF: 14:46 while `date -u` says 18:46), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/28-crop.png (twilight strip unchanged under Asia/Tokyo). sqlite3 confirms timezone/use_system_time persisted each time.
location_wrong: The cited root cause only half explains the symptom. clock_provider.dart:219 _parseTimezoneOffset does reject the 17 IANA names, but 'UTC' — the one entry it DOES parse (Duration.zero) — changes nothing either: with timezone=UTC and use_system_time=false the status-bar clock still read 12:04:44 host EDT instead of 16:04 UTC. The real cause for the cited surfaces is that they never consult clockProvider: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/widgets/status_bar.dart:188/200/209 uses raw DateTime.now(), and only 6 call sites app-wide read clockProvider. A fixer who only widened the parser per the finding's 'where' would leave the status bar and dashboard exactly as broken.
proposed_fix: Either store real IANA zones and resolve them with the `timezone` package (correct, handles DST), or change the picker to emit the UTC+HH:MM labels the parser already understands. At minimum make the fallback loud instead of silent.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on display :85, fresh profile. Site set to Seattle (47.6062/-122.3321/1234 m). (1) use_system_time OFF with timezone=UTC (DB confirmed): status-bar clock 12:04:44 while `date -u` = 16:04:44 — unchanged host-local. (2) Timezone = Asia/Tokyo (DB: timezone|Asia/Tokyo, use_system_time|false): status bar still 12:05:48 while `TZ=Asia/Tokyo date` = 01:05:48. (3) Dashboard Moon card byte-identical across both timezones (Moonrise 00:55 / Moonset 13:24). Picker is inert on every surface reachable. Severity: the control is dead and the app displays a timezone it does not honour, but nothing it computes is wrong-by-timezone (LST/twilight are longitude-driven; capture timestamps stay host-local and self-consistent) — a dead-setting/false-claim defect rather than a night-costing one, so P2.

title: The 'Maximum Quality' integration profile is a placebo -- it produces byte-identical settings to Balanced
what_happened: Selecting each of the five integration profiles in turn and diffing the whole ADVANCED block of the accessibility tree: Fast changes the resampler to Bilinear, Few Subs changes rejection to Percentile clip with 0.2/0.1, Long Night / Gradient changes normalization Mode from Global to Local grid -- but Balanced and Maximum Quality produce an IDENTICAL 30-line block (`diff bal.txt maxq.txt` is empty) and an identical summary sentence. The source confirms it: IntegrationSettings.preset(maximumQuality) sets resampler=lanczos3, weighting=snrSquared, generateRejectionMap=true, cosmeticCorrection=true, outputBitDepth=f32 -- every one of which is already the constructor default that balanced inherits. The only field that differs between the two presets is sourcePreset, which is a label.
expected: A profile named 'Maximum Quality' must actually cost something in exchange for quality -- e.g. a tighter RANSAC threshold, more reference stars, local normalization, linear-fit/percentile rejection tuned for the sub count, or drizzle. As shipped, a user who deliberately picks Maximum Quality over Balanced for their best data gets exactly the same stack and is misled about it.
repro: 1. Session Review > Workbench > Integration settings > expand Advanced settings. 2. Click 'Balanced', capture the ALIGNMENT..DRIZZLE block of `drive_linux.py tree`. 3. Click 'Maximum Quality', capture again. 4. diff -> no differences. 5. Repeat for 'Long Night / Gradient' -> exactly one line differs (Global -> Local grid), proving the capture method detects real changes.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/bal.txt vs /tmp/ns-audit/maxq.txt -> identical (30 lines each); /tmp/ns-audit/bal.txt vs /tmp/ns-audit/ln.txt -> 1 line differs. Summary line unchanged: 'Will integrate 9 accepted subs using Winsorized sigma. Recommends culling the worst 10%.' for both. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/integration_settings.dart:737-745 vs the constructor defaults at :672,:676,:690,:691,:692.
proposed_fix: Give maximumQuality settings that actually differ (e.g. ransacThresholdPx 1.5, maxRefStars 120, normalization local, reject linearFit) -- or drop the chip. Also make the panel's one-line summary mention the knobs the chosen profile changed, so three profiles cannot render the same sentence.
verdict_reasoning: Read the current source. integration_settings.dart:737 is exactly `case IntegrationPreset.maximumQuality:` returning const IntegrationSettings(resampler: lanczos3, weighting: snrSquared, generateRejectionMap: true, cosmeticCorrection: true, outputBitDepth: f32, sourcePreset: maximumQuality). All five are already the constructor defaults (:670 lanczos3, :674 snrSquared, :688 true, :689 true, :690 f32), and balanced at :733 is `const IntegrationSettings(sourcePreset: balanced)` i.e. all defaults. The two objects therefore differ only in sourcePreset, and the only non-test consumer of sourcePreset anywhere in packages/ or apps/ is integration_settings_panel.dart:51 `active: _s.sourcePreset`, which decides which chip is highlighted. Nothing in toBridgeSettings or the native path reads it. Cited file:line exact.

title: Confirming a First Light candidate does not update the Observing Alerts tab beside it: the same detection reads 'Confirmed' on one sub-tab and 'New' on the next
what_happened: On Analytics > Science > First Light I pressed Confirm on the candidate; the card's badge changed to 'Confirmed', the toast read 'Marked as confirmed.' and the database row updated (reviewed=1). Switching one tab across to Observing Alerts -- the same screen, the same detection, mapped through transientAlertFromDetection -- the card still carries a blue 'New' badge and sits under the 'New' filter. transientAlertFromDetection maps reviewed -> TransientAlertState.acknowledged, so the alert list is being served from a snapshot taken at app launch and is not rebuilt when the detection changes.
expected: Two views of one row, on two tabs of one screen, must not disagree. Confirming in First Light should immediately move the alert out of 'New'.
repro: 1. Seed a confirmed-able detection and restart the app. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light > Confirm (badge becomes 'Confirmed', toast 'Marked as confirmed.'). 3. sqlite3 -> reviewed=1. 4. Click 'Observing Alerts'. 5. The card shows the 'New' badge.
evidence: AT-SPI at 11:10 on First Light: 'Confirmed' twice plus 'panel: Marked as confirmed.'; DB at that instant: 1|newSource|1|0 (reviewed=1). /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-21.png at 11:14 on Observing Alerts: 'New' badge on the same detection. Mapping that should have produced 'acknowledged': packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper.dart:41-46.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_alert_provider.dart (the alert list is not invalidated when transient_detections changes)
location_wrong: Cause is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/transients/transients_screen.dart:122/143/167-172 + widgets/transient_card.dart:56 (card state comes from transientAlertStatesProvider; TransientAlert.state is ignored), NOT 'transient_alert_provider.dart -- the alert list is not invalidated'; the list IS re-merged via ref.listen at transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556.
proposed_fix: Have the alert provider watch the detections table (or invalidate it from the confirm/dismiss mutation) so both sub-tabs read one source of truth.
verdict_reasoning: Symptom REPRODUCED LIVE on the rebuilt bundle: seeded detection id 1 (newSource, reviewed=0), Analytics > Science > First Light > Confirm -> DB reviewed=1 and the card badge reads 'Confirmed' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-12.png); one tab across, Observing Alerts shows the same detection ('NS J13.50+47.2', Supernova) with a blue 'New' badge (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-11.png). But the finding's cause and 'where' are wrong, which matters because the cited file is not the one to fix. transient_alert_mapper.dart:66-70 does map reviewed -> acknowledged, and the list IS rebuilt: activeTransientAlertsProvider is a StreamProvider.autoDispose holding `ref.listen(allTransientDetectionsProvider, ...)` (transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556), and allTransientDetectionsProvider is a drift watchRecentDetections live query (transient_detections_provider.dart:95-100) that re-emits on the local markReviewed write. The badge stays 'New' because the Observing Alerts UI never reads the alert's own state: transients_screen.dart:122 watches transientAlertStatesProvider, :143 does `states[alert.id]`, and transient_card.dart:56 falls back to newAlert when that map has no entry; _filterAlerts :167-172 puts exactly those under 'New'. That map is only ever populated from persisted `transient_alert_state_<id>` settings rows written by the user's own queue/dismiss actions (:683-810) -- nothing seeds it from TransientAlert.state, so the mapper's `acknowledged` is dead on this surface.
